proof:
Source: steps 4 and 5 of the parent proof (radii; existence, location, normality and uniqueness of nearest points; the definition π := ψ∘pr₁∘Φ⁻¹), and steps 6(a), 6(b) and 7(a) (π is C¹ with values in N, π fixes N, and P̂(g(x))(x − π(x)) = 0). Notation: D(v) := Dψ(v), P̂(v) is the orthogonal projection onto range D(v), and y := ψ(v₀).
1. Normal coordinates. The sibling theorem Submission.dor_lmb_ret_normal_coordinates gives δ > 0, an open O ⊆ ℝ^P and g : ℝ^P → ℝ^d with B̄_δ(v₀) ⊆ V and g C¹ on O. They satisfy: for v ∈ B_δ(v₀) and n ∈ ℝ^P with P̂(v)n = 0 and |n| < δ, we have ψ(v) + n ∈ O and g(ψ(v) + n) = v.
2. Localization. ψ is continuous on V, since it is C² there. The sibling theorem Submission.dor_lmb_ret_chart_localization with ε := δ gives ρ₁ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ W and N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_δ(v₀)), such that K := N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁}(y) is compact. Since ψ(V) = W ∩ N, ψ(w) ∈ N for every w ∈ V; in particular y ∈ K.
3. Radius. Put r := min(ρ₁/2, δ) > 0. Fix x ∈ B_r(y) for steps 4–7.
4. Nearest point. The continuous function z ↦ |x − z| attains its minimum on the nonempty compact set K at some p ∈ K (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). As y ∈ K, |x − p| ≤ |x − y| < r. If z ∈ N ∖ K, then |z − y| > ρ₁, so |x − z| ≥ |z − y| − |x − y| > ρ₁ − r ≥ ρ₁/2 ≥ r > |x − p|. Hence |x − p| ≤ |x − z| for every z ∈ N.
5. Location. p ∈ K ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_δ(v₀)), so p = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and |v − v₀| < δ.
6. Normality. Let f(w) := |x − ψ(w)|². V is open and ψ is differentiable at v, so f is differentiable at v with Df(v)w = −2⟨x − ψ(v), D(v)w⟩ (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.norm_sq). For w in the neighbourhood V of v, ψ(w) ∈ N, so f(w) ≥ |x − p|² = f(v) by step 4. Thus f has a local minimum at v and Df(v) = 0 (Mathlib IsLocalMin.hasFDerivAt_eq_zero). So ν := x − p satisfies ⟨D(v)w, ν⟩ = 0 for all w ∈ ℝ^d. Hence ν ∈ (range D(v))^⊥ and P̂(v)ν = 0 (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_apply_eq_zero_iff).
7. Recovery. |ν| = |x − p| ≤ |x − y| < r ≤ δ, v ∈ B_δ(v₀) and P̂(v)ν = 0. Step 1 therefore gives x = ψ(v) + ν ∈ O and g(x) = v, so ψ(g(x)) = p.
8. Conclusions. By step 7, B_r(y) ⊆ O, so g is C¹ on B_r(y). For x ∈ B_r(y), with v, p, ν as above:
- g(x) = v ∈ B_δ(v₀);
- |x − ψ(g(x))| = |x − p| ≤ |x − z| for all z ∈ N, by step 4;
- P̂(g(x))(x − ψ(g(x))) = P̂(v)ν = 0, by step 6;
- if moreover x ∈ N, taking z := x gives |x − ψ(g(x))| ≤ 0, so ψ(g(x)) = x.
Together with 0 < r, 0 < δ and B̄_δ(v₀) ⊆ V (step 1), this proves the claim. ∎
key_steps: Normal coordinates (sibling) give δ, O, g with g(ψ(v) + n) = v for v ∈ B_δ(v₀) and normal n with |n| < δ. Chart localization (sibling) with ε = δ gives the compact piece K = N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁}(y) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_δ(v₀)).
For x ∈ B_r(y), r = min(ρ₁/2, δ), the distance from x to K is attained at some p; p is nearest among all of N, because points of N ∖ K are farther away.
p = ψ(v) with v ∈ B_δ(v₀), and the first-order condition for |x − ψ(·)|² at v gives x − p ⊥ range Dψ(v).
Recovery gives x ∈ O and g(x) = v. Hence g is C¹ on B_r(y), ψ∘g is the nearest-point map, normality holds, and points of N are fixed.
